description: Sync Freshdesk tickets and their replies from one helpdesk. Freshdesk ticket visibility is not imported.
opening: Sync every ticket in one Freshdesk helpdesk, with its replies. Each ticket is one document with its description, requester, assignee, company and group. Each reply is its own document, linked to its ticket.

Freshdesk agent scopes are not imported, so every synced ticket and reply is visible to everyone who can query the collection unless you set an access rule. Private agent notes are skipped unless you turn them on. Tickets deleted in Freshdesk stay in HydraDB. Attachments are not synced.

notes: Freshdesk Global, Group and Restricted agent scopes are not reproduced.
If you turn on `include_private_notes`, private agent notes are visible to everyone who can query the collection too.
Every ticket and reply carries `additional_metadata.rbac_warning`, saying that Freshdesk visibility is not captured.

connect.auth: Freshdesk uses an agent's API key and your helpdesk's subdomain.

credentials.name: api_key
credentials.text: An agent's API key, from the agent's Freshdesk profile settings.

credentials.name: domain
credentials.text: The helpdesk subdomain only, for example `acme` for `acme.freshdesk.com`.

credentials.name: include_private_notes
credentials.text: Off by default. Turn it on to also sync private agent notes.

connect.credentials_note: There is no scope to choose. The key reads the tickets its agent can see under that agent's Global, Group or Restricted ticket scope. Pick an agent with Global scope, or only part of the helpdesk syncs.

steps.title: Copy an agent API key
steps.text: In Freshdesk, open the profile settings of an agent with Global ticket scope and copy the API key.

steps.title: Create the connector
steps.text: Paste the key as `api_key` and the subdomain as `domain`. Turn on `include_private_notes` only if everyone who can query the collection may read private notes, or set an access rule.

steps.title: Configure the connector
steps.text: HydraDB lists one account-wide resource, All data. Select it to sync the whole helpdesk as one unit.

connect.account: One connector reads one Freshdesk helpdesk domain.

sync.first_sync: Reaches back the window set by `lookback_days`, 30 days by default.
sync.changes: Each sync reads tickets updated since the last sync, together with their replies. Replies are read again only when their ticket changes.
sync.edits: A changed ticket is read again with its replies and updates its documents.
sync.deletes: Deleted tickets are not removed. A ticket synced before it was deleted or marked as spam stays searchable in HydraDB.

shared_attributes.name: additional_metadata.freshdesk_id
shared_attributes.text: The ticket id on a ticket, the reply id on a reply. Targets one item, and keeps later syncs on the same document. Not searchable.

shared_attributes.name: additional_metadata.rbac_warning
shared_attributes.text: Set on every item, saying that Freshdesk visibility is not captured. Not searchable.

shared_attributes.name: connector_id
shared_attributes.text: Limits a query to this connector's items. Not searchable.

documents.name: Tickets
documents.one_document: One ticket. Spam and deleted tickets are skipped.
documents.title: The ticket subject.
documents.text: The plain-text description, converted from HTML when needed, or the subject when the description is empty. Then `Requester`, `Requester email`, `Assignee`, `Company` and `Group` lines. Status, priority and creation time are part of the text too. The subject is searchable too.
documents.date: When the ticket was last updated, else when it was created.
documents.link_back: The ticket in the Freshdesk agent portal.

attributes.name: status
attributes.text: Open, Pending, Resolved or Closed, written as a `Status` line. A custom status is written as its raw number.

attributes.name: priority
attributes.text: Low, Medium, High or Urgent, written as a `Priority` line.

attributes.name: requester
attributes.text: The requester's name, written as the `Requester` line, where HydraDB can identify the customer.

attributes.name: requester_email
attributes.text: The requester's email, written as the `Requester email` line, where HydraDB can connect the address to the customer.

attributes.name: assignee
attributes.text: The assigned agent's name or email, written as the `Assignee` line. The graph records the ticket as assigned to that agent.

attributes.name: company
attributes.text: The requester's company, written as the `Company` line, so every ticket from one company matches.

attributes.name: group
attributes.text: The name of the agent group the ticket is assigned to, written as the `Group` line.

attributes.name: created_at
attributes.text: When the ticket was created, written as a `Created` line. Used as the result date only when the update time is missing.

attributes.name: updated_at
attributes.text: When the ticket was last updated. Not searchable.

attributes.name: type
attributes.text: The Freshdesk ticket type.

attributes.name: tags
attributes.text: The ticket's tags.

attributes.name: requester_id
attributes.text: The requester's Freshdesk contact id.

attributes.name: responder_id
attributes.text: The assigned agent's id. The agent's name is in `assignee`.

attributes.name: group_id
attributes.text: The assigned group's id. The group's name is in `group`.

documents.name: Replies
documents.one_document: One reply or note on a ticket. Empty replies are skipped. Private agent notes are included only when `include_private_notes` is on.
documents.title: `Comment by` and the author's name. Without an author, the first 80 characters of the text.
documents.text: An `Author` line, then the plain-text reply. The creation and update times are part of the text too.
documents.date: When the reply was created, else when it was last updated.
documents.link_back: The parent ticket in the Freshdesk agent portal.

attributes.name: author
attributes.text: The agent who wrote the reply, written as the `Author` line. The graph records the reply as written by that agent. Customers are not named, because Freshdesk contacts are not synced.

attributes.name: from_email
attributes.text: The sender's email. Written as the `Author` line only when no agent name is found, which is the case for customer replies.

attributes.name: mentions
attributes.text: Names mentioned in a private note. The names stay in the note text, and the graph records each as mentioned.

attributes.name: parent_id
attributes.text: The ticket the reply belongs to. Links the reply to its ticket, so the whole conversation can be returned together.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.freshdesk_ticket_id
attributes.text: The id of the ticket the reply belongs to. Returns every reply on one ticket. Not searchable.

attributes.name: created_at
attributes.text: When the reply was created, written as a `Created` line.

attributes.name: updated_at
attributes.text: When the reply was last updated, written as an `Updated` line. Used as the result date only when the creation time is missing.

attributes.name: private
attributes.text: True for a private agent note. It does not restrict who can read the note.

attributes.name: incoming
attributes.text: True when the reply came from the requester, so you can tell a customer message from an agent reply.

attributes.name: author_id
attributes.text: The Freshdesk user id of the reply's author.

example_searches: What did an agent say about a billing issue?
Which urgent tickets are assigned to Priya?
Which tickets came from Acme Corp?

people: The assigned agent of each ticket.
The author of each agent reply.
Names mentioned in a private note.
The requester's name and email, and the company, appear in the ticket text, where HydraDB can identify them.
Customers who reply are not attached as people. Their email appears in the reply text.
graph.from_text: The ticket description with its requester, assignee, company and group lines, and the text of every reply.

not_synced: Private agent notes, unless `include_private_notes` is on.
Spam and deleted tickets. Replies on them can still be synced.
Contacts and companies as documents of their own.
Satisfaction ratings, time entries, solution articles and forum posts.
Deletions: tickets deleted in Freshdesk stay in HydraDB.
